bitcoin_core.why: latest tagged release at the time the harness was written; the coin-selection algorithms are used as-is, with only the instrumentation patch in patches/ applied

coin_select.describes: PR #76: a second, ancestry-aware greedy seed, on top of PR #75's sparse per-candidate ancestor sets and PR #73's depth-first branch and bound with the changeless metrics removed
coin_select.why: the ancestor-aware selection work this benchmark exists to measure, traversed depth-first (#73), with the per-candidate ancestor sets stored flat rather than as one dense bitset each (#75), and with a second greedy prefix ordered by (value - own bump) / weight kept whenever the metric scores it better (#76). #75 is what makes the scale tier in `bench.py scale` runnable at all: the dense form cost candidates x ancestors bits and the same in time to walk, putting a 200,000-candidate pool at 1.3 GB and 464 ms of setup before the first node. #76 is what the scale tier then found: past a hundred thousand candidates the search never improves on its seed, so the ancestry-blind sort order is the entire answer. It changes nothing on this 42-fixture matrix — all 42 selections are identical to #75's — and is pinned so the matrix stands as the evidence for that. `Changeless` and `LowestFeeChangeless` are still gone with #73, so the harness runs the wallet track alone
